question: Who is the main client for a community health nurse?

options.B: Only children under five years old
options.C: Patients admitted to the surgical ward

explanation: You've got this! While ward nurses care for one patient at a time, community health nurses look out for whole neighborhoods and populations.

question: How is community health nursing different from working in a hospital ward?

options.A: It emphasizes disease prevention and health promotion in local settings
options.B: It deals exclusively with rare surgical procedures
options.C: It restricts care strictly to indoor clinic rooms
options.D: It relies entirely on high-tech diagnostic machinery

explanation: Spot on! Hospital nursing handles sick individuals, but community nursing goes out to homes and public spaces to keep everyone healthy.

question: Back in the Middle Ages, who mainly cared for and sheltered the sick?
explanation: Monks and nuns played a huge role early on, setting up early sanctuaries to offer food, shelter, and basic care.

question: What was the main drive behind early caregiving in ancient and medieval times?
explanation: Great job! Long before professional licenses and paychecks, early caregivers were driven by faith and a deep moral duty to help the vulnerable.

question: Who started the first district nursing scheme in Liverpool to care for poor families right in their homes?
explanation: William Rathbone teamed up with nurses to organize home care for sick people who couldn't afford a hospital, creating the district nursing model.

question: A public health nurse visits a crowded urban settlement to improve sanitation and teach hygiene. Whose historical footsteps is this nurse following?
explanation: Lillian Wald is a legend in public health! She took nursing straight into busy neighborhoods to tackle health and social needs together.

question: What was a major focus of early community health efforts during the colonial days in Nigeria?
explanation: Early health programs had to tackle heavy burdens like malaria and smallpox that were affecting local populations.

question: Why did Nigerian health planners eventually shift their focus toward rural communities?

options.A: Rural areas had no traditional healers left
options.B: Urban residents refused to visit government hospitals
options.C: The majority of the population lived in rural areas with limited medical access
options.D: Colonial laws prohibited urban healthcare expansion

explanation: That makes total sense—since most people lived outside the cities without clinics nearby, health services had to reach out to the grassroots.

question: Which international declaration in 1978 made Primary Health Care the main strategy for global health?
explanation: Remember Alma-Ata! The 1978 conference put Primary Health Care on the map as the key to health for everyone.

question: What key lesson did the world learn from successful global vaccination campaigns against smallpox?

options.A: Coordinated international public health strategies can eradicate major diseases
options.B: Vaccines are only effective inside sterile hospital operating rooms
options.C: Local communities cannot participate in disease prevention
options.D: Infectious diseases disappear naturally without human intervention

explanation: Teamwork works! Smallpox proved that when the whole world joins forces on immunization, we can wipe out deadly diseases.

question: What is a major downside of a healthcare system that focuses only on big hospitals?

options.A: It provides too many vaccines directly inside family homes
options.B: It neglects preventive care and ignores rural or poor communities
options.C: It focuses too much on keeping people healthy
options.D: It relies entirely on community health workers instead of doctors

explanation: Exactly. When everything is locked inside city hospitals, people in remote areas miss out on basic checkups and early care.

question: Why did public health systems move away from just hospital care and embrace Primary Health Care?

options.A: To eliminate the need for any nurses or doctors in rural areas
options.B: To make hospital buildings larger and more expensive to run
options.C: To ensure that only wealthy citizens receive medical treatments
options.D: To make healthcare more accessible, preventive, and community-focused

explanation: Spot on! Primary Health Care brings services right to the people, stopping sickness before it ever needs a hospital bed.

question: Which of these is NOT a current challenge facing community health nurses in Nigeria?

options.A: Funding shortages for public health programs
options.C: The double burden of infectious and non-communicable diseases
options.D: Zero prevalence of any health problems in the country

explanation: You got it! Nigeria definitely still deals with various health challenges, so saying there are zero problems isn't true.

question: A community health nurse in rural Nigeria uses a mobile phone app to track children's immunizations. What does this show?

options.A: The integration of technology into modern community health practice
options.B: A complete return to medieval religious care giving methods
options.C: The abandonment of primary healthcare principles
options.D: An illegal practice that violates public health policies

explanation: Just like you using this CBT app on your phone, modern nurses use digital tools every day to make healthcare smarter and faster!
